question.text: Two bodies, each of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math>, are kept fixed with a separation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>L</mi></math>. A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is projected from the midpoint of the line joining their centers, perpendicular to the line. The gravitational constant is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>G</mi></math>. The correct statement (s) is (are) :

options.text: The minimum initial velocity of the mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> to escape the gravitational field of the two bodies is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mi>G</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow><mi>L</mi></mfrac></msqrt></math>.

The minimum initial velocity of the mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> to escape the gravitational field of the two bodies is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mi>G</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow><mi>L</mi></mfrac></msqrt></math>.

The minimum initial velocity of the mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> to escape the gravitational field of the two bodies is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>G</mi><mi>M</mi></mrow><mi>L</mi></mfrac></msqrt></math>.
The energy of the mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> remains constant.
